paragraphs: All the Tannaim and Amoraim whose father's name was Yosef.
Rav Acha bar Yosef, [Shabbat 110b:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.110b.3), or the son of Rav Yosef, [Eruvin 29b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.29b.5).
Rav Hamnuna son of Rav Yosef, [Berakhot 24b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.24b.5).[^6]
Rav Chana bar Yosef, Taanit ch. 4, end of halakhah 5.
Rav Chama bar Yosef, [Shabbat 7b:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.7b.3)[^5], or the son of Rav Yosef, Eruvin 65b, according to the reading of Dikdukei Soferim.[^7]
[Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.11b.22), Berakhot 9b. Mar son of Rav Yosef, [Shabbat 116a:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.116a.10).
[Rav Nechemya son of Rav Yosef](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.28a.20), Shabbat 3b. Sumchos bar Yosef, the well-known.
Rav Anan bar Yosef, Midrash Tehillim, ch. 65, section 4.
Rabbi Akiva bar Yosef, the well-known.
Rav Papa son of Rav Yosef, [Bava Metzia 113a:11](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.113a.11). Rabbah bar Yosef, [Arakhin 5b:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Arakhin.5b.3).[^4]

notes.text: This notice lists people by their father-name Yosef; it does not identify all those fathers with one another. The source prints Midrash Tehillim65:4.
An earlier editorial comparison proposed chapter68 for the Midrash Tehillim reference; the supplied notice gives65:4, which is retained here.

Berakhot 45b directly names Rav Dimi bar Yosef. This corroborates that listed patronymic, not a single shared father for all the people in the index. The consulted Berakhot 24b passage gives the shorter Hamnuna without the patronymic; it does not independently verify the supplied Hamnuna bar Yosef form.

The consulted Midrash Tehillim explicitly gives Rav Anan bar Yosef among those transmitting in Rav Idi’s name. Berakhot 24b gives the school of Rav Hamnuna without the patronymic. The entry is a name list. The linked Eruvin 65b passage shows Rav Yosef and Rabbah in Rav Sheshet’s academy; it does not verify the patronymics ascribed to that folio. See also [Eruvin 65b (Rav Yosef)](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.65b.4-5), [Midrash Tehillim 65:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Midrash_Tehillim.65.4).

At [Shabbat 7b:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.7b.3) the consulted edition names Rav Chiyya bar Yosef where Hyman lists Chama. [Ketubot 111b:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.111b.9) also names Chiyya bar Yosef. The cited passage of [Eruvin 65b:19-21](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.65b.19-21) names Chanina bar Yosef. [Chullin 31b:12-13](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.31b.12-13) names Yonatan ben Yosef, while [Berakhot 47b:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.47b.6) names Natan bar Yosef in a different discussion. [Berakhot 11b:22](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.11b.22) gives Yitzchak bar Yosef. [Shabbat 116a:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.116a.10) reads Mar bar Yosef, while [Niddah 44b:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.44b.4) has Mar son of Rav Yosef. The account naming Rav Nechemya son of Rav Yosef continues at [Beitzah 28b:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.28b.1). The Rav Papa passage is at [Bava Metzia 113a:11](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.113a.11) in the consulted edition, with Nachman or Yosef as alternate father names. The links on Chiyya, Yonatan, Yitzchak and Nechemya give other attestations of the cited names. Hyman cites Shabbat 115b for Mar and Bava Metzia 113b for Papa.

[Berakhot 24a:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.24a.4) explicitly names Rav Hamnuna son of Rav Yosef in an incident before Rava. The consulted passage at Hyman’s supplied 24b gives the shorter name.

The consulted [Eruvin 65b:19](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.65b.19) names Rabbi Chanina bar Yosef in the inn case. The alternate reading about Rav Chama is Hyman’s report from Dikdukei Soferim and remains unconfirmed in that edition.
